concepts.title: the snack-table volunteer
concepts.premise: LABEL: FICTIONAL/STAGED — Maria discovers that her boyfriend volunteered both of them to handle his younger sister’s club snack table before asking her.
concepts.hook_direction: A group-thread screenshot raises the question of why he volunteered her so confidently.
concepts.action_trigger: His sister shares his RSVP in the family group chat.
concepts.human_event: He made a public promise on their behalf, then reveals he had quietly collected the club’s food restrictions because he knew Maria would not want anyone excluded.
concepts.stakes: Maria has to decide whether the thoughtful preparation outweighs being volunteered without consent.
concepts.expected_consequence: They either make the event work together or he has to own the overstep in front of his family.
concepts.reveal: The practical work was real care, but it does not erase the fact that he should have asked first.
concepts.proof_surface_direction: group thread; notes-list artifact; native order artifact; candid snack-table photo
concepts.payoff: A warm but debatable recovery rather than a clean romantic win.
concepts.primary_comment_door: is it sweet if he did all that homework, or still annoying because he volunteered her?
secondary_comment_doors: which food restriction is easiest to forget when planning for a group?
concepts.commerce_relation: OUTCOME-MEANS — only pursue if later boundary mapping shows a natural order changes not-enough-to-enough for the actual club need; any program evidence remains a staged native discount line on an order surface, never a character explanation.
concepts.why_it_fits_account: A low-stakes couple disagreement anchored in recognizable teen-family food logistics.
risks: Could feel like a food argument if the relationship tension overtakes the public-volunteering issue.
The food quantity must arise from the event, never from discount headroom.
research_needed: Verify a plausible, natural group-order boundary and normal ordering path before commercial synthesis.
Verify that the selected food and event details fit current teen-life behavior.

concepts.title: the finals-night elevator delay
concepts.premise: LABEL: FICTIONAL/STAGED — A first-year roommate’s family arrives to help move her out, but everyone is trapped waiting on an overloaded dorm elevator while the roommate tries not to cry about leaving.
concepts.hook_direction: A lock-screen preview announces that the family has arrived just as the roommate says she cannot do a goodbye speech.
concepts.action_trigger: The family reaches the dorm early and the move-out plan stalls.
concepts.human_event: Maria turns the forced wait into one final floor hangout so the roommate does not have to face a formal goodbye alone.
concepts.stakes: The roommate wants a normal last memory, not a tearful scene in front of her parents and the whole floor.
concepts.expected_consequence: The improvised hangout either gives her a softer goodbye or makes the departure feel even more real.
concepts.reveal: The people waiting with her had already made a tiny goodbye ritual without telling her.
concepts.proof_surface_direction: lock-screen preview; roommate group thread; native order artifact; camera-roll hallway photo
concepts.payoff: An unexpectedly intimate, slightly chaotic final dorm-floor memory.
concepts.primary_comment_door: would you want everyone to make a big deal out of leaving, or pretend it is a normal night?
secondary_comment_doors: is an improvised goodbye better than a planned one?
concepts.commerce_relation: ARTIFACT — the food order belongs to the stalled hangout; a later staged order artifact may create a separate method-gap question, but it does not explain the goodbye.
concepts.why_it_fits_account: It stays inside the first-year-college phone life-world and lets food support a real emotional event instead of replacing it.
risks: Must not imply that a commerce artifact caused the emotional resolution.
Avoid making move-out logistics look implausibly dramatic.
research_needed: Verify normal dorm move-out constraints and a credible food-order timing path.
Research whether a material economic boundary exists without inventing one.

concepts.title: the sleepover guest list changed at 10:48
concepts.premise: LABEL: FICTIONAL/STAGED — Maria agrees to a quiet cousin sleepover, then learns that her cousin invited the entire friend group because one girl is newly avoiding a fight at home.
concepts.hook_direction: A family text says the guest count changed, but not why.
concepts.action_trigger: Maria’s younger cousin sends a panicked update after the friends have already arrived.
concepts.human_event: The bigger group is not a planned party; it is a last-minute attempt to give one friend a safe, ordinary night.
concepts.stakes: Maria must protect the cousin’s trust without making the guest feel like a charity case.
concepts.expected_consequence: The group either settles into a believable normal sleepover or the secret becomes the center of the night.
concepts.reveal: The cousin planned the inflated guest list so no one would notice which friend needed somewhere else to be.
concepts.proof_surface_direction: family text thread; cousin group-chat fragment; native order artifact; low-light living-room photo
concepts.payoff: The sleepover becomes caring because it stays ordinary.
concepts.primary_comment_door: would you tell the host why you needed to stay over, or let a friend cover for you?
secondary_comment_doors: what makes a sleepover feel normal when someone is having a bad night?
would your family notice an extra group immediately?
concepts.commerce_relation: OUTCOME-MEANS — only if later boundary mapping supports a natural transition from insufficient food for a quiet sleepover to enough for the real group need. The order cannot be padded or treated as the reason the friend feels safe.
concepts.why_it_fits_account: A recognizable high-school group dynamic with food as a natural hosting need and a meaningful viewer judgment.
viral_texture_opportunities: blankets and shoes by the door
risks: Handle the home-conflict context lightly; it cannot become trauma bait.
The food must remain secondary to the cousin’s protective choice.
research_needed: Research a credible, non-exploitative framing for a teen needing an ordinary night away from family conflict.
Verify a natural group-order boundary and realistic delivery chronology.

concepts.title: the spicy-food alibi
concepts.premise: LABEL: FICTIONAL/STAGED — Maria realizes her boyfriend has let his relatives believe she dislikes spicy food because it has been his easiest excuse for years to skip dishes he hates.
concepts.hook_direction: A family dinner photo makes it look like Maria is the reason he ordered a separate comfort meal.
concepts.action_trigger: A relative tags Maria in a joke about finally getting him to eat plain food.
concepts.human_event: Maria has to decide whether to expose the harmless lie or let him keep the alibi at the next family dinner.
concepts.stakes: The joke is small, but it turns Maria into the person his family thinks changed him.
concepts.expected_consequence: His relatives either learn the truth or keep treating Maria as the explanation for his preferences.
concepts.reveal: He has always avoided those foods; Maria only noticed he never corrected the story.
concepts.proof_surface_direction: family photo; tagged comment; saved-menu note; casual camera-roll payoff
concepts.payoff: A tiny couple truth that invites judgment without needing a villain.
concepts.primary_comment_door: would you expose him immediately or let him keep the alibi?
secondary_comment_doors: what food opinion do people blame on your partner?
is this a harmless cover story or unfair to her?
concepts.commerce_relation: ABSENT — organic-only. Do not force program economics into this premise.
concepts.why_it_fits_account: It is a casual food-and-couples observation with an easy, culturally familiar comment split.
risks: Must not turn into a generic food argument.
No campaign production unless later work finds a genuine, non-forced economic job.
research_needed: Research needed only if later adapting actual food, restaurant, or ordering behavior.

concepts.title: the post-exam comfort spread
concepts.premise: LABEL: FICTIONAL/STAGED — After a friend leaves an exam convinced she failed, her friends build a deliberately unserious movie-night comfort spread without letting her know they saw her crying.
concepts.hook_direction: A close-friends message asks for one very specific kind of ‘do not ask questions’ night.
concepts.action_trigger: The friend sends a single-word update after the exam and goes quiet.
concepts.human_event: Her friends coordinate an attainable sleepover-style reset instead of giving advice she does not want.
concepts.stakes: They want to show up without embarrassing her or making the bad exam the theme of the night.
concepts.expected_consequence: The friend either feels cared for by the ordinary ritual or realizes everyone saw more than she wanted them to.
concepts.reveal: Each person brought one detail from a comfort routine she had mentioned at different times.
concepts.proof_surface_direction: close-friends thread; shared list artifact; native order artifact; camera-roll movie-night photo
concepts.payoff: The desired outcome is a specific, savable feeling of being looked after rather than a product reveal.
concepts.primary_comment_door: what is the correct food for a ‘do not ask me about it’ night?
secondary_comment_doors: would you want friends to acknowledge the bad exam or distract you?
what tiny detail makes a comfort night feel thoughtful?
concepts.commerce_relation: ABSENT — preserve as organic desire/utility material unless later research identifies a natural qualitative boundary; cheaper same outcome is not a usable job.
concepts.why_it_fits_account: A highly recognizable 15–20 food ritual with outcome desire and a method gap that work without economics.
risks: Family D evidence is thin, so treat this as lower confidence.
Do not make the friend’s distress performative or turn the spread into a purchase showcase.
research_needed: Research whether the chosen comfort-food details are current and naturally attainable for the intended age group.
Research needed before assigning any commerce relation beyond ABSENT.
